blocks.text: 11-ADC / ad copy Goes here. A tutorial on using AI (specifically ChatGPT-4.5) to write direct-response advertorials. It covers a five-step framework: deep research, creating foundational documents (avatar sheet, offer brief, necessary beliefs), swiping competitors, AI drafting, and the "chiefing" (editing) process. Not here. • Landing page UX design or conversion rate optimization -> 07-LPG • Paid media campaign setup or Facebook Ad buying -> 10-MCR

Header. url: rights: public_reference why: Provides a highly structured, prompt-engineering blueprint for generating long-form direct-response copy (advertorials) using AI, emphasizing the necessity of feeding the LLM deep qualitative research rather than just asking it to rewrite existing copy. modules: [ADC] topics: [advertorials, copywriting, ChatGPT, deep research, avatar sheet, offer brief, necessary beliefs, AI prompting, direct response, chiefing] tier: 3 scope_hint: comprehensive

Topics. the fatal flaw in AI copywriting / explaining that simply asking ChatGPT to rewrite a competitor's ad without feeding it foundational research results in terrible, low-converting copy; the five-step advertorial framework / outlining the process: (1) Research via AI, (2) Foundational Docs, (3) Swipe an existing competitor, (4) Write the advertorial, and (5) Chief (edit) the copy; feeding context to AI / demonstrating how to convert a brand's sales page into a PDF and upload it to ChatGPT to ground the AI in specific product details before prompting; ChatGPT's Deep Research feature / using AI to write its own deep research prompt to crawl the web for customer pain points, generating a massive qualitative research document in 10-15 minutes; building foundational documents / turning the raw research into three specific PDFs: an Avatar Sheet (demographics, pain points, direct quotes), an Offer Brief (funnel architecture, stage of awareness, unique mechanism), and a Necessary Beliefs doc (the specific mindset shifts required for a customer to buy); swiping and drafting / uploading a successful competitor's advertorial as a structural reference (the "swipe"), and prompting the AI to write the new advertorial in chunks (first half, then second half) to bypass token limits and ensure high quality; the slippery slide principle / referencing the copywriting rule that copy must flow so naturally that the reader slides down it without friction; the AI "chiefing" process / uploading the final drafted advertorial back into ChatGPT to evaluate it against the foundational documents, ensuring it hits all necessary beliefs, unique mechanisms, and objection handling before human editing.

The Deep Research AI Inception: The specific prompt-engineering tactic where you ask ChatGPT to write the prompt that will be used to trigger its own "Deep Research" feature, ensuring the most comprehensive data scrape possible.

Token Limit Chunking: The rule that you must never ask an LLM to write a full 2,000-word advertorial in one prompt due to token limits drastically lowering the output quality; always prompt it to write the "first half," review it, and then prompt the "second half."

The Slippery Slide Copywriting Principle: The editorial benchmark that copy must flow so naturally and logically that the prospect slides from the headline to the Call to Action without hitting any "bumps" (illogical phrasing or friction).

The Necessary Beliefs Document: A foundational copywriting asset outlining a maximum of six specific beliefs a prospect must hold to positively buy the product (e.g., "I believe my current method is inefficient").

Skip. Plugs for the creator's swipe file, generic rants about why ChatGPT is better than Claude, and mentions of specific product details (e.g., the space heater example) that don't serve the broader prompt-engineering lesson.

Scope mix. 15% baseline (basic definitions of advertorials), 85% growth (advanced AI prompt engineering, qualitative research methodologies, and direct-response copywriting frameworks). Volume. ~400 words.
